name: Don Carlos Smith
role: Youngest brother of Joseph Smith and Nauvoo editor
dateNote: He was named president of the high priests in section 124 in January 1841 and died that August.
importance: Section 124 names him “Don C. Smith” as president over a quorum of high priests, with Amasa Lyman and Noah Packard as counselors. He had first been chosen to lead the high priests in Kirtland in 1836. He also edited the Church newspaper Times and Seasons from 1839. He died of pneumonia at Nauvoo on 7 August 1841, aged twenty-five.
connections: Son of Joseph Smith Sr. and Lucy Mack Smith and youngest brother of Joseph and Hyrum. His daughter Ina Coolbrith became a California poet.
reviewNote: Dates, baptism (9 June 1830), high priest presidency, editorship, and cause of death from Wikipedia; the JSP person page did not load. The D&C names him only as “Don C. Smith” (124:133).
